The plaint averments in brief are that, the plaintiff No. 1 is a foreign company incorporated in Malaysia and plaintiff No. 2 is a company incorporated in India, under the Companies Act 1956. The plaintiff No. 1 and 2 entered into joint venture agreement dated 05-07-2001 and the sole object of t h e s a i d j o i n t v e n t u r e [ h e r e i n a f t e r r e f e r r e d t o a s J V ] w a s C T 1390_Com.O.S.7734-2014_Judgment.doc KABC170099392020 to submit bid for a tender floated by defendant No. 1 / National Highway Authority of India [hereinafter referred to as NHAI]. It is stated that although the nomenclature of the p r o j e c t w a s r e h a b i l i t a t i o n a n d u p g r a d a t i o n o f t h e N a t i o n a l H i g h w a y t h e C T 1390_Com.O.S.7734-2014_Judgment.doc KABC170099392020 said nomenclature was not totally apposite since the work included in the project involved not only rehabilitation of existing two lanes but construction of additional two lanes with provision for service roads, widening of existing slab culverts, widening of existing minor bridges and construction of new minor bridges, construction of vehicular and non- vehicular underpasses, construction of grade separators, junctions, road appurtenances, drainage and protective works and also preparatory works like site clearance and cutting of trees. I n o t h e r w o r d s , t h e t i m e p e r i o d c o n t e m p l a t e d u n d e r t h e C T 1390_Com.O.S.7734-2014_Judgment.doc KABC170099392020 contract for completion of the work was 2.5 years or 30 months.
texts.facts: It is specifically pleaded that, as a result of delay in handing over the land to the plaintiffs, there was delay / prolongation of one and half years which compelled the plaintiffs to keep their men and materials in ready state to work in full capacity as a result of which the plaintiffs have suffered loss and therefore for elongation period of one and half years, the plaintiffs are entitled to 10% of the contract price for additional head office overheads and 10% of the contract price for loss of profits and CT 1390_Com.O.S.7734-2014_Judgment.doc KABC170099392020 thereby by applying the Hudson's formula, it is contended that plaintiffs are entitled to recover Rs. 23,58,52,935 from the defendants for the delay in handing over the site which led to prolongation of the work. The plaintiffs continued to claim reclassification of ordinary rock and hard rock and increase in the rates for hard rock and ordinary rock excavation. because the defendants claimed that excess payments had been made to the plaintiffs and deducted the said excess payments from the payments to be made to subcontractor. In the meantime, plaintiff No. 1 independently filed another WP No. 5766-2006 for quashing the termination of the contract and refund of amount of bank guarantee encashed and for declaring clause 52.2 of Conditions of Contract as unconstitutional and arbitrary. However, on 18- 05-2006, since there was no stay in the matter, the defendant No. 1 expelled the plaintiffs from the project site. Challenging the same, Plaintiff No. 1 filed Writ Appeal 4504 of 2009 and the Division Bench of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka [LEAKAGE_MASK] the orders of the learned single judge and relegated the parties to approach competent court of law. On the basis of the said orders in Writ Appeal, the plaintiffs are before this Court for the following reliefs; a) For declaration that termination of the contract by the defendants is illegal and arbitrary b) Declaration that encashment of the bank guarantees by defendants is illegal and without authority of law. The plaintiffs were dissatisfied with the decision of the DAB and sought arbitration and issued arbitration notice dated 15-04- 2005 and plaintiffs claimed that towards the additional rate for rock excavation, the plaintiffs are entitled to recover Rs. 14,64,06,350 from the defendants. At this stage, due to the financial strain caused to the JV on account of failure of Defendants to pay amounts due and due to the increase in the quantity of rock excavation, the plaintiffs by themselves could not carry on the balance work and therefore the balance work left over in the project was entrusted to subcontractor namely Associated Constructions under subcontract agreement. At this stage, the defendants did not permit the subcontractor to complete the work because the defendants claimed that excess payments had been made to the plaintiffs and deducted the said excess payments from the payments to be made to subcontractor. As a result of the same, the subcontractor suspended the work. At that stage, the defendants issued notice to the plaintiffs under clause CT 1390_Com.O.S.7734-2014_Judgment.doc KABC170099392020 63.1 of the General Conditions of Contract, alleging that plaintiffs had not shown significant progress in the performance of the work and if improvement is not made within 25 days, the contract would be terminated, vide letter dated 19-08-2005 and in a meeting dated 15-09-2005, the defendants directed the plaintiffs to submit proposal for completion of the project, including getting a new contractor, on or before 27-09-2005, failing which the defendants would terminate the contract and expel the plaintiffs from the site and invoke the bank guarantees. Challenging the same, Plaintiff No. 1 filed Writ Appeal 4504 of 2009 and the Division Bench of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka [LEAKAGE_MASK] the orders of the learned single judge and relegated the parties to approach competent court of law. On the basis of the said orders in Writ Appeal, the plaintiffs are before this Court for the following reliefs; a) For declaration that termination of the contract by the defendants is illegal and arbitrary b) Declaration that encashment of the bank guarantees by defendants is illegal and without authority of law. The learned single judge on same ground relegated the parties to arbitration and the division bench in writ appeal [LEAKAGE_MASK] the said orders and relegated the parties to civil court.
texts.arguments: What is contended by the appellant is that the said clause is arbitrary and declaration is sought to the effect that proviso to clause 52.2 of the contract is illegal, arbitrary, unreasonable and fraudulent and violative of Article 14 of the Constitution to the extent that clause 52.2 is interpreted as permitting a contractor to claim varied rates for additional works only if the relevant item of additional work amounts to more than 2% of the contract price in the original Bill of Quantities and directing that the contractor be reasonably compensated for the additional works in accordance with paragraph 58 of the petition and therefore, in order to adjudicate the dispute b e t w e e n t h e p a r t i e s , i t i s n e c e s s a r y t o g o i n t o t h e s e r i o u s l y d i s p u t e d C T 1390_Com.O.S.7734-2014_Judgment.doc KABC170099392020 questions of fact which can be done only by the Court of competent jurisdiction by recording evidence and this Court cannot resolve the said dispute which involves seriously disputed questions of fact by exercising writ jurisdiction of this Court. The defendants being statutory authority cannot be expected to do any act contrary to the contract. Therefore, the plaintiffs have failed to prove that second proviso to clause 52.2 is fraudulent and once this conclusion is reached, it follows that the plaintiffs are not entitled to any additional rates for excavation of work which is specifically barred by clause 52.2 and therefore, the plaintiffs cannot take the same as a ground for non-completion of the work.
